item.text: Cultures share the same sunrise and sunset, but they organize time around different needs and meanings. Farming, prayer, trade, work routines, climate, technology, and social customs can make certain moments especially important. One society may emphasize dawn, noon, and dusk; another may use watches, market hours, or ritual intervals. Language and historical traditions also shape which boundaries feel natural, so the same physical day can be divided in culturally distinct ways.
